holds.excerpt: Diagnose whether the encoder motor runs when a shift is commanded;
Diagnose with a scanner (encoder position codes).
codes must be cleared with a scan tool after replacement or the case may not shift correctly.
After replacement, a battery sensor reset via a scan tool is required.
Test the system by engaging 4WD on a loose surface.
Test for leaks with a fuel pressure gauge before closing up.
Diagnose heater control module and PTC heater element.
Because sender failure is common, replacing the full module usually restores both fuel delivery and gauge accuracy;
on dual-tank trucks, also test the tank selector valve for proper switching and fuel flow because a failed valve can mimic pump failure and cause starvation.
a known-good remote-mounted PMD test module is often the quickest confirmation.
run the proper 12-gauge switched feed to the HEI.
Before converting an old distributor, do the 'wiggle test' on the shaft;
Pressure/UV-dye test to locate the leak.
Diagnosis usually starts with a persistent misfire, ticking, and cylinder-specific contribution loss;
Scan for P2135 (and related P2101/pedal codes).
Scan for correlation codes and compare camshaft actual vs.
Diagnose fuel-rail pressure with a scan tool;
Coolant system pressure test to find leaks.
Scan the EBCM for wheel speed sensor data and compare all four wheel speeds during a slow stop.
If the new resistor fails again quickly, the blower motor should be amperage-tested and replaced if current draw is excessive.
If DEF quality warning appears, have system diagnosed - may need sensor replacement.
Test and replace the failed cooling fan relay and/or coolant temperature sensor — both are inexpensive parts.
For fuel-gauge creep and wrong FUEL RATE readings, repair the ground wire at the center lock pillar on coupes.
replace the fuel-level sending unit if gauge readings are off.
Compare Bank 2 upstream vs downstream O2 sensor data on a scan tool — a downstream sensor that switches rapidly with the upstream one indicates a worn converter;
Have an oil-consumption test performed (documented quart-per-mile measurement) to qualify for goodwill/settlement coverage.
Replace the purge or vent solenoid only if the smoke test localizes the leak there;
Scan the TCM (not just generic powertrain codes) to retrieve the companion code — most commonly P0741 on this platform, or a shift-solenoid code.
Scan and record all emissions DTCs (e.g., P11DB, P249D) and freeze-frame data.
Diagnose by graphing fuel-level sender voltage vs.
Re-test by flooding each drain corner with water and confirming it exits underneath.
Scan for specific wheel speed sensor codes to identify which corner has failed.
gauge: an erratic/fluctuating needle points to the fuel level sensor/sending unit, while a gauge that won't rest at E (key off) or reach F (full tank) points to the gauge/cluster.
Scan for throttle/pedal DTCs before replacing parts.
Diagnosis is usually straightforward when turn signals work intermittently and the fault changes when the hazard switch is pressed or wiggled.
Have the EPS motor and torque sensor diagnosed with a scan tool — the module stores specific fault codes.
Bleeding the ABS system requires a scan tool to cycle the pump and valves.
Diagnose the vacuum circuit and replace the failed actuator, cracked vacuum lines, and/or transfer-case vacuum switch.
A spider-plug/fuel-pressure test isolates a leaking poppet before replacement.
If the gauge itself doesn't respond when the sensor is unplugged, the instrument-cluster stepper motor is the culprit instead.
Don't replace the oil pump on a bad-reading gauge alone.
Diagnose with a running-compression test on the misfiring cylinder (an AFM lifter that stays below ~25 PSI regardless of solenoid command is collapsed).
Out-of-recall vehicles experiencing a hard pedal should have the vacuum pump tested and replaced if output is low, and the oil change interval kept current to limit sludge.
Scan for stored codes (commonly P2138 and related APP/throttle codes) and read live throttle/pedal data.
Diagnose lifter/misfire with a scan tool;
Load-test the battery and clean/tighten the terminals and negative ground.
Scan for the specific reductant/NOx code before parts.
Scan for codes (P1098 / P26BB are commonly reported);
After replacement, use a scan tool to relearn the encoder motor position.
Replace glow plug controller module if diagnostics indicate module failure.
Clear adaptation values with scan tool.
Diagnose the specific fault code to determine which DEF component failed.
Have the specific DTC codes read with a proper scan tool (not just a basic code reader).
If transmission slipping or shuddering begins, have it diagnosed immediately before complete failure occurs.
Persistent, worsening, or hot-running knock should be diagnosed to rule out a real bearing/rod knock;
A scan tool is needed to program the new module to the BCM after installation.
Diagnose first with a line-pressure test in reverse to separate hydraulic (valve body/servo) from mechanical (sunshell/clutch) causes.
Diagnose with a fuel-pressure gauge (pressure that bleeds down after shutoff points to leaking poppets).
Retrieve codes to isolate the branch: P1515/P1516 point at the TAC/throttle actuator, P2135/P0120-series at the TPS/APP correlation.
First rule out a blown fuel-gauge/sender fuse and attempt a scan-tool sensor recalibration.
If the gauge is still erratic, replace the fuel level sending unit — on high-mileage trucks replace the complete in-tank fuel pump module (ACDelco/Delphi module) since the pump often follows.
if gears merely lost sync a scan-tool relearn can sometimes clear it without parts.
Test 4WD engagement monthly to keep actuator exercised.
Diagnose the hydraulic power steering system for pressure loss;
Have the system evacuated and dye/pressure leak-tested.
Diagnose and replace the failed HVAC blend door actuator(s) for the affected zone, then recalibrate the climate system.
the second bulletin addresses the no-crank codes with module diagnosis and reprogramming.

Always pull DTCs first — wheel speed sensor codes point to a sensor/tone-ring replacement, while misfire codes (P0300-series) mean the StabiliTrak light is secondary and the misfire/ignition cause must be fixed.
Resist clearing the light without diagnosis;
if the concern persists, diagnosis focuses on display, radio, or communication faults on the infotainment network.
Repeated jump-starting without root-cause diagnosis can mask the actual draw problem.
Diagnosis should include verifying camera power/ground, coax or video signal integrity, and whether the issue is isolated to the camera or part of a broader infotainment dropout.
If software updates do not resolve it, dealers may replace the camera or radio/display components depending on test results.
